answer: The passages describe several appeal routes for a refused long-stay visa. First, you can file an informal appeal (recours gracieux) with the consulate, asking it to reconsider its decision. Second, you can refer the matter to the Commission de recours contre les décisions de refus de visa d'entrée en France (CRRV), but only by mail. This CRRV appeal is mandatory before you can go to the administrative court, and you must file it within 30 days of written notification of the refusal (or of an implicit refusal, if the consulate has not replied within 2 months). Your appeal must state the legal and factual grounds, be written in French, be signed, and include any useful documents. If the CRRV rejects your appeal, or if the ministers uphold the refusal despite a favourable CRRV opinion, you can bring an annulment appeal within 2 months before the administrative court of Nantes. The passages do not say whether a student visa has any different rules from other long-stay visas.
